newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Jutrzenka seeks large investor.
newsitem.headline: Polish Jutrzenka seeks large investor.

text.p: Polish confectioner Przedsiebiorstwo Cukierniczne Jutrzenka SA (Jutrzenka) is seeking a strategic or financial investor to take a minority share, the firm's president said on Wednesday.

"We want to gain a big investor or investors who would affirm that Jutrzenka is a serious firm...currently no one at Jutrzenka holds more than five percent of shareholder votes," Grzegorz Dolkowski told Reuters.
He said the majority of the company would still be held by its founders, management and employees.

Dolkowski said Jutrzenka was negotiating with four potential foreign and domestic financial investors and two international confectioners already active in Poland but not competing directly with Jutrzenka.
He said concrete offers would be submitted in October and that a share price for the financial investors would be struck through book building.
Dolkowski said proceeds from the issue would go toward new technology, the building of a plant and the upgrading of four plants at Jutrzenka's base in Bydgoszcz, northern Poland.
"We want to find and outside source of capital which in 1997 and 1998 would allow us to invest more than last year," he said.
The company invested 20 million zlotys last year and plans to invest 9.3 million this year.

Jutrzenka, which netted 7.1 million zlotys last year and 5.9 million through the first eight months of 1996, seeks to transfer next year to the Warsaw bourse's main market from the parallel floor where smaller, less liquid issues are traded.
